newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end quiet day mixed to weaker.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end quiet day mixed to weaker.

text.p: At the end of pit trading, IMM currency futures were mixed to weaker following a day of quiet consolidation from Tuesday's extreme volatility.
Traders and analysts expect two or three more days of moderate activity as markets sort out the impact of major declines in December sterling and December Australian dollars early in the week.

The U.S. dollar's rally against European currencies was reined in by a stock market reversal that saw the Dow Jones industrial average off nearly 40 points in late trading, as well as by stabilization in the sterling, one trader said.

Amid lower gold prices and heavy cash cross action, markets have focused on remarks by former Reserve Bank of Australia governor Bernie Fraser that the last Australian interest rate cut was too small. Fraser's comment suggested to some traders that further rate cuts may be in store.
For December marks and December Swiss francs, extended downtrends are intact, one technical analyst said. Both contracts finished Wednesday slightly off.
December yen seesawed most of the day to close below Tuesday's high. "You continue to see some yen movement in the crosses, particularly against the D-mark," a trader said.
Still, one technical analyst predicted, "The decline isn't over for sterling."
In the next few days, he said, "I would look for a bounce to $1.6550 and then a move down into the area between $1.6250 and $1.6300."
One trader said, "They're pretty much done with the corrective phase (in sterling), but I don't think they're going to generate a whole lot of new interest in it."
December Australian dollars erased some of Tuesday's heavy losses to finish with a gain, but one analyst said, "In Australia, you have to talk about lower interest rates there."

"There's talk that the (Japanese Ministry of Finance) is sending signals that they don't want the (cash) dollar-yen above 115.00 and that continues to generate speculation of short-covering in the yen," the trader added.
Wednesday's release of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book and the Boskin Commission's report on the U.S. Consumer Price Index had no discernible impact on currency futures.

Markets were looking toward Friday's release of November payrolls data, forecast to non-farm payrolls rising by 179,000 jobs after October's rise of 210,000, with the jobless rate expected to hold steady at 5.2 percent.
Strong data would buoy the dollar, although the payroll report's impact likely will be muted by recent Euro-cross volatility, a trader said.

At the end of pit trade, December yen were up $0.000017 at $0.008858, marks were off 0.0016 at $0.6414, Swiss francs were off $0.0002 at $0.7580, sterling was unchanged at $1.6428, Canadian dollars were off $0.0020 at $0.7392, Australian dollars were up $0.0076 at $0.7989 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000050 at $0.125950.
